# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 30 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 30 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_030_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 3, continued — On Falsehood in Business

**1** "Now I command you: love truthfulness. Guard it so that it remains with you always. **2** Beloved, let only what is worthy of God proceed from your mouth, and let no falsehood whatsoever enter it. **3** You were commanded to love truthfulness; so love it and hold fast to it." **4** I said, "Sir, in our business dealings and other transactions we sometimes speak falsely — not because we want to sin, but because we are compelled. Can we be saved?" **5** He replied, "You will be saved if you do not do so willfully. Those who speak a false word willfully are the ones who sin. But those who are compelled and speak falsely involuntarily do not sin greatly; and if they repent, it will be forgiven them. **6** But the one who lies voluntarily harms himself, because such conduct has become his way of life. You, then, be on guard concerning this commandment, and keep it, that you may not bring harm upon yourself."

---

*LOGOS note: The distinction between voluntary and compelled lying is a significant early Christian contribution to moral theology. The Shepherd anticipates the kind of moral reasoning that would become systematic in later patristic ethics.*
